gen_risks.description: Severe flooding during construction could damage bridge foundations and delay works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply flood‑resilient design, schedule critical works outside peak rainy season, and install temporary cofferdams.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 2.1 description of flood‑adaptation measures for bridges (Annex 5).

gen_risks.description: Extreme heat may cause premature deterioration of road and bridge pavements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use heat‑resistant materials, incorporate expansion joints, and specify thermal design limits in specifications.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 5 climate‑adaptation measures mention weather‑resistant materials for bridges and roads.

gen_risks.description: Fragmented institutional responsibilities could lead to coordination failures among ministries and agencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen NPSC oversight, define clear roles in the Project Implementation Manual, and hold monthly coordination meetings.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 15 notes institutional fragmentation and overlapping responsibilities.

gen_risks.description: The PCIU lacks an established procurement unit and qualified staff, risking ineffective procurement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified procurement specialists before effectiveness, provide World Bank procurement training, and set up a record‑keeping system.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 6 procurement risk assessment: “PCIU is yet to be established and the capacity of procurement staff… low.”

gen_risks.description: MTA’s limited experience with World Bank financial‑management procedures may cause compliance gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire a FM specialist, develop a FM manual, and conduct targeted FM training for staff.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 7 FM assessment cites “Insufficient experience of MTA with the World Bank’s FM procedures.”

gen_risks.description: A US$7.1 million financing gap for four SCADeP bridges could postpone their completion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure the GoSL’s pledged fiscal contribution, explore private‑sector bridge financing, and activate contingency funds if needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 2 sub‑component b description of the US$7.1 m gap and GoSL commitment.

gen_risks.description: Prolonged rainy seasons may suspend civil works, extending the project schedule.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt incremental launching construction method, build weather buffers into the timeline, and monitor forecasts closely.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 9 notes the incremental launching method to avoid delays from rainy seasons.

gen_risks.description: Corruption or fraud in procurement could inflate costs and undermine project integrity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement transparent bidding, use STEP for monitoring, enforce anti‑corruption training, and conduct regular PPRs.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 6 lists fraud and corruption risks and mitigation measures.

gen_risks.description: Limited competition in tendering may lead to higher prices and lower quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Aggregate small packages, run outreach to private sector, and publish clear tender documents.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 6 procurement risk assessment mentions “Insufficient competition in procurement.”

gen_risks.description: Absence of a systematic road‑safety database hampers evidence‑based safety policy.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a national road‑safety information system and integrate data collection into the RAMS platform.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 8 states “There is no systematic database on road safety.”

gen_risks.description: Gender gaps may limit women’s access to transport services and market facilities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate gender‑sensitive design (lighting, sidewalks, women‑only spaces), set hiring targets, and run outreach through women’s groups.
gen_risks.evidence: Gender sections describe gender‑informed designs for components 1‑3.

gen_risks.description: Low mobile‑phone penetration among rural women could reduce uptake of the AMIS mobile app.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide community‑based information channels, conduct digital‑literacy trainings, and use radio/TV to disseminate market data.
gen_risks.evidence: Section on AMIS notes limited phone access for rural women and need for alternative channels.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient post‑completion funding may jeopardize bridge and road maintenance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish bridge management system with cost‑recovery mechanisms, train local councils on revenue collection, and embed O&M budgets in RMFA.
gen_risks.evidence: Critical Assumption 2: “Funding is available and project bridges and link roads are adequately maintained after project closing.”

gen_risks.description: Increased flood frequency could cause scour around bridge piers, threatening structural integrity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design with right‑sized drains, install scour protection, and schedule regular underwater inspections.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 2.1 design includes scour protection and flood‑resilient standards.

gen_risks.description: Unclear CERC activation procedures may delay emergency response funding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finalize CERC manual and Emergency Action Plan before implementation, train staff on trigger criteria.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 5 description of CERC and need for manual.

gen_risks.description: Delay in establishing the National Project Steering Committee could weaken project oversight.
gen_risks.mitigation: Meet the 60‑day covenant, allocate resources, and appoint members promptly after effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal covenants schedule 2, Section I.A.2(a) require NPSC within 60 days.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate climate data may lead to under‑designed flood protection for bridges.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use climate‑proofed design parameters, update flood quantification methods, and apply safety factors.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 5 notes need to factor climate change into design flood levels.

gen_risks.description: Bus fleet expansion may not keep pace with rising urban travel demand, worsening congestion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement lease‑operate‑own scheme, prioritize bus lanes, and regularly update demand forecasts.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1 sub‑component c describes fleet renewal and demand growth to 750,000 trips/day by 2033.

gen_risks.description: If market infrastructure is delayed, post‑harvest losses could remain high, reducing farmer incomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fast‑track construction, monitor milestones weekly, and allocate contingency funds for critical path items.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 3 notes post‑harvest losses of 20‑30 % and need for timely market upgrades.

gen_risks.description: Sexual harassment incidents on public transport may deter women’s use of services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Install CCTV on buses, set up a hotline, conduct SH awareness training for operators.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1 sub‑component c mentions CCTV and SH response measures.

gen_risks.description: Weak grievance redress mechanisms could lead to community dissatisfaction and project delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a transparent GRM, publicize procedures, and ensure timely response within set timelines.
gen_risks.evidence: Section V outlines Grievance Redress Services.

gen_risks.description: High inflation and fiscal pressures may erode real project costs and affect budgeting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include cost‑escalation clauses, monitor macro‑economic indicators, and adjust budgets annually.
gen_risks.evidence: Country Context notes “soaring inflation driven by global supply shocks” and fiscal pressures.

gen_risks.description: Limited capacity of local contractors may affect construction quality and timelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct pre‑qualification, provide technical training, and assign qualified supervision consultants.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 6 procurement risk assessment cites “lack of knowledge in using World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.”

gen_risks.description: Zero‑emission bus technology may be infeasible, limiting GHG mitigation benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Perform feasibility study, adopt hybrid or high‑efficiency diesel buses if electric not viable, and revisit later.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1 notes bus fleet may use zero‑emission or hybrid buses if technically feasible.

gen_risks.description: Weak data management for BMS/RAMS could impair asset‑management decisions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop GIS‑based BMS, train staff, and integrate with RAMS for real‑time monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 2 sub‑component c describes establishment of climate‑resilient BMS.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance is rated Substantial. This project's activities are not highly sensitive to moderate perturbations in the political dispensation, although pronounced degeneration in political stability could still undermine their implementation. The more likely risk is that poor governance may affect implementation for the road sector, resulting in reduced commitment during implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated through close supervision, strict adherence to the criteria for beneficiary selection, and fiduciary oversight.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed as Substantial. Sierra Leone's post-pandemic recovery was disrupted by concurrent domestic and external shocks. Inflation and exchange rate depreciation reached record levels, depressing economic activity and triggering a severe cost-of-living crisis. Fiscal accounts have deteriorated on account of macroeconomic headwinds and policy slippages, and risks to debt sustainability have intensified. The economy is projected to grow at 3.8 percent on average during 2023-2025, below the long-term trend, and this baseline is vulnerable to downside risks given recent fiscal slippages and expenditure overruns. The macroeconomic risk may raise concerns about contractors' cost overrun and delay of payment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Key macroeconomic reforms will help reduce the imbalances and avoid the downside risks. The project is 100 percent financed by IDA which will help mitigate the macroeconomic challenges to project implementation.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. The key fiduciary risks are related to the overall governance context of the project, the risk that procurement of project works may be delayed and/or result in higher-than-expected bid prices or poorly performing contractors, and difficulty retaining qualified procurement and FM professionals in the PCIU.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated by implementing an action plan that aims to strengthen the accountability and control framework for project implementation and improve overall fiduciary performance, and by ensuring adequate procurement and FM training. The PPSD will establish appropriate prequalification requirements and adopt standard lessons from experience procuring similar works contracts in Sierra Leone. The FM risk will be further mitigated by recruiting an internal auditor under PCIU.

gt_risks.description: The project's E&S risk is Substantial (para 74, explicitly pointing to section V.D for detail - para 74 states both environment risk and social risk are rated Substantial 'as indicated in section V.D'). Section V.D (paras 64-68): overall E&S risk classification is Substantial, with eight of ten Environmental and Social Standards (ESS) applying. Environmental risk is Substantial: construction activities are expected to generate air/noise nuisance, construction waste, and traffic/worker safety issues, and Component 2 in particular could affect downstream water users (water quality/hydrology, navigation, fish catch, riparian vegetation), with some impacts potentially long-term or irreversible (e.g. accidental spill of used oil/electrolytes/hazardous materials into the river during construction). Social risk is also Substantial: key risks include physical and economic displacement of boat/ferry operators, loaders, and traders after bridge construction; SEA/SH risks from the contractor workforce; elite capture in market-infrastructure interventions; social exclusion of vulnerable groups (persons with disabilities, women/small traders, the landless, elders); and secondary risks including potential child labor, communicable-disease spread from the contractor workforce, and local conflict over benefit-sharing from downstream impacts.
gt_risks.mitigation: Standard measures per the ESIA/ESMP to be prepared for project activities, including energy-efficiency measures per World Bank EHS Guidelines/GIIPs; a site-specific SEA/SH risk assessment and commensurate GBV/SEA/SH action plan; the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) and Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), disclosed April 19, 2024; hiring a social specialist with GBV/SEA/SH experience before project effectiveness; an ESIA and Resettlement Action Plan/livelihoods restoration plan already under development for the seven originally-planned bridges, with updated ESIA/ESMP/RAP and a SEA/SH action plan to be disclosed within one month of effectiveness; and a functional grievance mechanism (GM) plus Labor Management Procedures (LMP) for project workers.
